The moving crossover cancels in differentiation. On s>1/sqrt(1+t²), x=s sqrt(1+t²) yields xP′/(4r)=G_t(x), whose positive t sqrt(x²−1) increases while the other positive integral decreases, establishing strict monotonicity and at most one interior minimum. Endpoint derivative at s=1 equals H(t)=sqrt(1+t²)−asinh(1/t), strictly increasing across one zero. The stated unique side-on vs tilted minimizer, equality cases, smooth-root near threshold yielding square-root angular cusp, and t→infinity expansion follow. value.rationale: The bicone is a canonical symmetric nonpolyhedral convex body. Finding the direction that minimizes its shadow perimeter, including a unique geometric bifurcation between side-on and oblique, has clear geometric optimization content: exact full-domain threshold, global uniqueness and critical square-root law. These are not automatic consequences of generic projection formulas or arbitrary numerical minimization.
